messages.subject: ODE solver
parts:
Hi,

Can somebody help me to speed up Stan simulation which uses ODE solver? I am working with a large PBPK (Physiologically Based PharmacoKinetic) model. At first I simulate the data and afterwards I try to estimate single parameter - R code as well as stan code to simulate the data and estimate parameter is attached. 

Also, since the same ODE model is used to generate the data and for estimation purposes it would be great to have include statement in stan - perhaps for next release.

Thanks for advice.

Linas

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: ODE solver
parts:
Hi Linas!

Whow, what a huge model! There are a couple of things you should (probably have to) consider:

- To my knowledge rstan supports an include functionality and for cmdstan you can find on this list a trick I published to make includes work as well

- Instead of includes I would recommend you to use the expose_stan_function in R. So you need to add a function, calculate_pred, or so which calculates y_hat for your model. Then you can export that to R and just call the function

- The most important one: Do not pass this huge vector into the ODE as parameters, but instead only pass the 1 parameter which you really want to estimate as parameter into the ODE RHS function!! All parameters which are constant should be passed into the function via x_r, the real array intended for data.

This last thing has to do with the fact that Stan is calculating internally gradients of the ODE solution with respect to the parameters. The ODE RHS function assumes that everything what you pass into it as 3. argument to be a parameter for which sensitivities are calculated. Getting those sensitivities is insanely numerically expensive and you should always try to keep the size of the array in the 3. argument position as small as possible and instead use the x_r for anything which does not change. You could, for example, use the x_i as int array to indicate which index in the parameter vector is varying, just an idea.

Note that Stan´s capabilities wrt to ODEs are getting much improved in the upcoming versions.

Best,
Sebastian
